3: Even though the Shulchan Arukh ruled in siman 689 in accordance with the opinion of Bahag that woman do not enable men to fulfill their obligation of reading Megila. Despite the fact that women are obligated in the mitzva of Megila, that case is different than our own. Regarding the reading of Megila, there are opinions that women do not make a blessing over the "reading" of Megila; rather, their blessing is over "hearing" Megila, as the Beit Yosef says there. Therefore, it would certainly be incorrect, ab initio, for them to discharge a man's obligation. That is not the case here, however, as all admit there is no distinction whatsoever between men and women...
